united-kingdom.visaNotes: Students need a CAS (Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies) from their university, proof of tuition plus maintenance funds held for 28 consecutive days, payment of the Immigration Health Surcharge, and completion of the Student visa application with biometrics at a VFS appointment.
united-kingdom.languageNotes: English is the language of instruction throughout. Bachelor's applicants need IELTS 6.0–6.5 (UKVI) or equivalent SELT, while master's applicants need IELTS 6.5 (typically 6.0 in each band).
united-kingdom.costNotes: Tuition is £15,000–35,000/yr overall (undergraduate £15,000–30,000/yr, postgraduate taught £16,000–35,000/yr), with maintenance funds of £13,347 (London) or £10,224 (outside London) for 9 months and an Immigration Health Surcharge of £776/yr. Estimated cost of living is ~£1,300/month, with students typically needing £1,100–1,500/month.
united-kingdom.workRights: The Graduate Route currently offers 2 years of post-study work (3 years for PhD graduates), reducing from January 2027 to 18 months for bachelor's and taught master's graduates. Students may work up to 20 hours a week during term time and full-time in holidays, and can later switch to a Skilled Worker visa with a qualifying job offer.
united-kingdom.tagline: The UK combines globally respected degrees with a clear post-study work pathway.

ireland.visaNotes: Students need to accept their offer and pay a tuition deposit, show proof of funds (~€10,000), arrange private medical insurance, complete the Irish student (Study) visa application with documents and biometrics submitted at a VFS centre, and register for an Irish Residence Permit (IRP) after arrival.
ireland.languageNotes: English is the language of instruction throughout. Bachelor's applicants need IELTS 6.0–6.5 / TOEFL or equivalent, while master's applicants need IELTS 6.5 with no band below 6.0.
ireland.costNotes: Non-EU tuition is €9,850–25,000/yr (undergraduate) and €10,000–35,000/yr (postgraduate taught), with proof of funds required at ~€10,000/yr. Estimated cost of living is ~€1,000/month, with students typically needing €1,000–1,300/month.
ireland.workRights: The Third Level Graduate Scheme allows students to stay to seek work for 12 months (Level 8) or 24 months (Level 9/10), with a Critical Skills Permit available as a fast-track route for in-demand roles. Students may work 20 hours a week in term time and 40 hours during holidays.
ireland.tagline: Ireland blends globally recognised degrees with a clear graduate work pathway inside the EU.

canada.visaNotes: Students need a Letter of Acceptance (and a Provincial/Territorial Attestation Letter where required), a GIC or verified proof of funds (CAD 22,895), and must complete the study permit application on the IRCC portal with biometrics at a VFS centre and any required medical exam. From 2026, master's and doctoral students at public institutions are exempt from the study-permit cap.
canada.languageNotes: Bachelor's applicants need IELTS 6.0–6.5 / TOEFL / PTE, while master's applicants need IELTS 6.5, with GRE/GMAT required for some programmes.
canada.costNotes: Tuition is CAD 15,000–35,000/yr (undergraduate), CAD 17,000–45,000+/yr (postgraduate) and CAD 13,000–22,000/yr (colleges/diplomas), with a GIC of CAD 20,635 and an updated living-cost proof figure of CAD 22,895/yr. Estimated cost of living is ~CAD 1,900/month, with students typically needing CAD 1,700–2,200/month.
canada.workRights: The Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP) offers up to 3 years of post-study work, with master's graduates getting 3 years; Express Entry provides a route towards permanent residence. Students may work up to 24 hours a week off-campus during study terms, and co-op programmes offer paid work placements during study.
canada.tagline: Canada offers world-class education with a clear path to work and settlement.

australia.visaNotes: Students need a Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE), a Genuine Student (GS) statement and documents, proof of funds covering tuition, travel and AUD 29,710 in living costs, and Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC), before lodging the subclass 500 student visa application online. The 485 graduate-visa fee rose to AUD 4,600 from March 2026.
australia.languageNotes: English is the language of instruction throughout. Bachelor's applicants need IELTS 6.0–6.5 / TOEFL / PTE and must meet the Genuine Student (GS) requirement, while master's applicants need IELTS 6.5 with no band below 6.0 (plus relevant work experience for some MBA courses).
australia.costNotes: Tuition is AUD 20,000–45,000/yr (undergraduate), AUD 22,000–50,000/yr (postgraduate) and AUD 8,000–22,000/yr (vocational/VET), with mandatory OSHC of AUD 500–700/yr and a living proof-of-funds figure of AUD 29,710/yr. Estimated cost of living is ~AUD 2,400/month, with students typically needing AUD 2,200–2,800/month.
australia.workRights: The Temporary Graduate (485) visa offers 2–3 years of post-study work, longer for research and regional study, with a Regional Bonus giving additional post-study time for regional study, and Skilled Migration providing a pathway towards permanent residence. Students may work up to 48 hours per fortnight during study and full-time during breaks.
australia.tagline: Australia combines world-ranked degrees with generous post-study work rights.

united-states.visaNotes: The F-1 visa process involves accepting your offer to receive the Form I-20, paying the I-901 SEVIS fee, completing the DS-160 form, paying the visa fee and scheduling an appointment, and attending an F-1 visa interview at a US consulate. Applicants must show funds covering the full tuition and living costs listed on the I-20.
united-states.languageNotes: For bachelor's admission, SAT/ACT (where required) and TOEFL 80+ / IELTS 6.5 are required; for master's admission, GRE/GMAT are required for many programmes along with TOEFL 90+ / IELTS 6.5–7.0.
united-states.costNotes: Indicative tuition is $28,000–80,000/yr overall, broken down as: Undergraduate (public, international) $28,000–45,000/yr, Undergraduate (private) $50,000–80,000/yr, Postgraduate/Master's $30,000–70,000/yr, and Community college $10,000–20,000/yr. Proof of funds (I-20) must cover the full annual cost, and estimated monthly cost of living is ~$1,500–2,500.
united-states.workRights: F-1 students can work 20 hours a week on campus during term, use CPT for internships during study, and access OPT for 12 months of post-study work in their field, plus an additional 24 months under STEM OPT for STEM graduates (36 months total).
united-states.tagline: The USA offers the world's largest choice of universities and a STEM work pathway of up to 3 years.

new-zealand.visaNotes: The visa process involves accepting your offer and paying fees, showing NZD 20,000 in proof of funds to cover living costs, completing medical and police (health & character) checks, submitting the Immigration NZ student visa application online, and arranging approved travel and health insurance.
new-zealand.languageNotes: Bachelor's applicants need IELTS 6.0 (no band below 5.5); master's applicants need IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0).
new-zealand.costNotes: Tuition is indicated as NZD 22,000–45,000/yr overall, broken down as: Undergraduate NZD 22,000–35,000/yr, Postgraduate/Master's NZD 26,000–45,000/yr, Medicine & specialist "higher, varies", and MBA (full programme) NZD 40,000–65,000. Proof of funds for the visa is NZD 20,000/yr, and estimated monthly cost of living is ~NZD 1,800–2,400.
new-zealand.workRights: Students work 20 hours a week in term, then graduates can access a Post-Study Work Visa of up to 3 years (open work rights for eligible graduates), a new Short-term Graduate Visa of 6 months (from Nov 2026, for lower-level qualifications), and a points-based Skilled Migrant residence route.
new-zealand.tagline: New Zealand pairs globally ranked degrees with one of the most generous post-study work visas.

singapore.visaNotes: The process involves accepting your offer and paying a deposit, having the institution register your Student's Pass via SOLAR, completing the online E-Form 16 application, completing a required medical exam, and collecting your Student's Pass from ICA on arrival.
singapore.languageNotes: Bachelor's applicants need IELTS 6.0–6.5 or equivalent; master's applicants need IELTS 6.5, with GMAT/GRE required for some programmes.
singapore.costNotes: Tuition is indicated as S$17,000–50,000/yr overall, broken down as: Undergraduate (with MOE grant) S$17,000–30,000/yr, Undergraduate (no grant) S$30,000–50,000/yr, Postgraduate/Master's S$25,000–55,000/yr, and Private institutions S$15,000–40,000/yr. Proof of funds for the pass is ~S$12,000, and estimated monthly cost of living is ~S$1,600–2,600.
singapore.workRights: Public-university students may work 16 hours a week (permitted at approved autonomous universities), and graduates get a Long-Term Visit Pass of 12 months to seek work; the main graduate work route is the Employment Pass (S$5,600+ salary), with the S Pass as a mid-skilled route.
singapore.tagline: Singapore offers world-top-20 universities in a safe, English-speaking business hub close to India.

japan.visaNotes: The process involves the university applying for your Certificate of Eligibility (COE), applying at the Japanese consulate with your COE, submitting required documents and photos, receiving approval and travelling to Japan, and collecting your residence card and joining the national health insurance scheme on arrival.
japan.languageNotes: For bachelor's programmes, IELTS 6.0/TOEFL is required for English-taught courses, or JLPT N2 for Japanese-taught courses, with an entrance exam (EJU) for some programmes; for master's programmes, IELTS 6.0+ or JLPT proficiency is required.
japan.costNotes: Tuition ranges from ¥535,800 (flat rate at national universities) up to ¥1,500,000/yr, broken down as: National universities ¥535,800/yr, Public universities ¥535,800–650,000/yr, Private universities ¥800,000–1,500,000/yr, plus a one-off admission fee of ~¥282,000. Proof of funds required is ~¥2,000,000, and estimated monthly cost of living is ~¥90,000–140,000.
japan.workRights: Students may work 28 hours a week with a work-outside-status permit; graduates get up to 1 year to job-hunt under a Designated Activities (Job-Hunting) visa, with a skilled Work Visa route via Engineer/Specialist in Humanities status.
japan.tagline: Japan offers affordable national universities, world-class engineering and a 1-year job-hunting visa.

france.visaNotes: Applicants complete the Campus France "Études en France" procedure and academic interview, secure an admission letter, and show proof of funds of around €615/month (~€7,380/year) before applying for the long-stay student visa (VLS-TS) via VFS; the visa must be validated online within three months of arrival and students must register with French student social security.
france.languageNotes: English-taught bachelor's courses require IELTS 6.0–6.5 or TOEFL, while French-taught bachelor's programmes require DELF/DALF B2; master's programmes require IELTS 6.5 or TOEFL (GRE/GMAT for some programmes), with French proficiency needed for French-taught master's.
france.costNotes: Public university tuition (non-EU rate) is €2,902/year for a Bachelor's and €3,941/year for a Master's, plus a ~€100/year CVEC student and campus contribution; grandes écoles and private schools range €3,000–20,000/year; proof of funds for the visa is ~€615/month (~€7,380/year); estimated cost of living is ~€1,000/month, with students typically needing €900–1,100/month.
france.workRights: Master's graduates can access a 24-month stay-back permit (APS) to find work or start a business, with a Talent Passport route offering a multi-year residence permit for qualified graduates and professionals; students may work up to 964 hours per year (about 20 hours a week) alongside their studies.
france.tagline: France blends academic prestige with strong industry and research links across Europe.

italy.visaNotes: Applicants complete Universitaly pre-enrolment online, secure an admission letter, and show proof of funds of around €6,900 for the year before submitting a national (Type D) long-stay student visa application via VFS; on arrival they must arrange health insurance/register with the national health service and apply for a permesso di soggiorno within 8 days of arrival.
italy.languageNotes: English-taught bachelor's courses require IELTS 6.0–6.5 or TOEFL, while Italian-taught programmes require Italian B1–B2; entrance tests apply for some programmes such as design and medicine; master's programmes require IELTS 6.5 or TOEFL (GRE/GMAT for some), Italian proficiency for Italian-taught master's, and a portfolio for design and architecture.
italy.costNotes: Public university tuition is income-based (ISEE) at €900–4,000/year, plus a regional tax of €140–200/year; polytechnics and private schools cost €4,000–20,000/year and fashion/design academies are higher and vary; proof of funds for the visa is ~€6,900/year; estimated cost of living is ~€900/month, with students typically needing €800–1,000/month.
italy.workRights: Graduates can access a 12-month job-search permit to look for work or start a business, with the option to convert the student permit to a work permit once employed; students may work up to 20 hours a week (around 1,040 hours a year) alongside studies.
italy.tagline: Italy pairs world-leading design and engineering with centuries of academic tradition.

poland.visaNotes: Applicants secure an admission letter from a Polish university, show proof of funds of around PLN 12,800 for the year, arrange health insurance, and submit a national (Type D) long-stay student visa application via VFS with proof of accommodation; a temporary residence card is required after arrival for longer stays.
poland.languageNotes: English-taught bachelor's courses require IELTS 6.0–6.5 or TOEFL, with medical programmes requiring an entrance exam and science subjects; Polish proficiency is required only for Polish-taught programmes; master's programmes require IELTS 6.5 or TOEFL (some require GRE/GMAT), with Polish proficiency needed for Polish-taught master's.
poland.costNotes: Tuition for most bachelor's and master's programmes is PLN 8,000–17,000/year; engineering & IT is PLN 12,000–20,000/year; medicine (MD/MBBS) is PLN 40,000–65,000/year, approximately €2,000–4,000/year for non-medical programmes; proof of funds for the visa is ~PLN 12,800/year; estimated cost of living is ~PLN 3,000/month, with students typically needing PLN 2,500–3,500/month (~€550–750).
poland.workRights: Graduates can access a post-study permit (about 9 months) to look for work, with a route to convert to a work permit once they have a qualifying job offer; from July 2026, students can work without a permit only if their university is on the government's approved list, otherwise a work permit is required.
poland.tagline: Poland offers affordable, EU-recognised education in the heart of central Europe.

hungary.visaNotes: Applicants secure an admission letter from a Hungarian university, show proof of funds to cover living and tuition costs, arrange health insurance, and apply for a study residence permit via VFS, providing biometrics and documents; registration must be completed after arrival.
hungary.languageNotes: English-taught bachelor's courses require IELTS 6.0–6.5 or TOEFL, with an entrance exam required for medicine and some programmes; master's programmes require IELTS 6.5 for most courses, along with a motivation letter and references.
hungary.costNotes: Bachelor's and master's tuition is €3,000–8,000/year; medicine/dentistry is €12,000–16,000/year; engineering & IT is €4,000–8,000/year; a one-off application/registration fee is €100–200; proof of funds for the permit varies; estimated cost of living is ~€650/month, with students typically needing €600–800/month.
hungary.workRights: Graduates can access a 9-month post-study permit to seek work, with a route to convert to a work permit once employed; students may work up to 24 hours a week during term time.
hungary.tagline: Hungary offers affordable, EU-recognised education, especially in medicine and engineering.

austria.visaNotes: The visa process involves securing an admission letter, showing proof of funds around €11,000, arranging health insurance, applying for a student residence permit via VFS, providing biometrics, and registering after arrival. Non-EU students may work up to 20 hours a week with a work permit during study.
austria.languageNotes: IELTS 6.0–6.5 or TOEFL is required for English-taught bachelor's courses, with German B2 for German-taught programmes; IELTS 6.5 is required for English-taught master's, with German proficiency needed for German-taught master's.
austria.costNotes: Public university tuition (non-EU) is ~€1,453/yr; Universities of Applied Sciences cost €3,600–14,000/yr; private universities cost €6,000–20,000/yr; the student union (ÖH) fee is ~€25/semester; proof of funds required is ~€11,000/yr; estimated monthly cost of living is ~€950 (students typically need €900–1,100/month).
austria.workRights: Graduates can obtain a 12-month Post-Study Permit (residence permit to seek work after study), and the Red-White-Red Card offers a points-based skilled work and residence route. Non-EU students may work up to 20 hours a week with a work permit during study.
austria.tagline: Austria offers low-fee public universities and an outstanding quality of life.

finland.visaNotes: The visa process involves securing an admission letter, showing proof of funds around €6,720, arranging health insurance, applying for a student residence permit online, providing biometrics at a VFS centre, and registering after arrival.
finland.languageNotes: IELTS 6.0–6.5 or TOEFL is required for bachelor's applicants (some programmes also require an entrance exam or task), and IELTS 6.5 is required for most master's programmes.
finland.costNotes: Bachelor's tuition (non-EU) is €8,000–12,000/yr and master's tuition (non-EU) is €10,000–18,000/yr; scholarships commonly cover 50–100% of tuition; proof of funds required is ~€6,720/yr; estimated monthly cost of living is ~€850 (students typically need €800–1,000/month).
finland.workRights: Graduates can obtain a 2-year Post-Study Permit (residence permit to seek work after study). Students may work up to about 30 hours a week during study.
finland.tagline: Finland pairs world-class technology education with generous tuition scholarships.

sweden.visaNotes: The visa process involves accepting the offer and paying the first tuition instalment, showing proof of funds of ~SEK 10,314/month, applying for a student residence permit online, providing passport/admission/funds documents, giving biometrics at a VFS centre if required, then receiving a decision and planning travel.
sweden.languageNotes: IELTS 6.0–6.5 or TOEFL is required for bachelor's applicants, and IELTS 6.5 (typically 5.5 in each band) is required for master's applicants.
sweden.costNotes: Bachelor's tuition (non-EU) is SEK 80,000–145,000/yr and master's tuition (non-EU) is SEK 100,000–160,000/yr (approx. €7,000–14,000); the application fee is SEK 900 (one-off); proof of funds required is ~SEK 10,314/month; estimated monthly cost of living total is ~SEK 10,300 (students need SEK 10,000–12,000/month).
sweden.workRights: Graduates can obtain a 1-year Post-Study Permit (residence permit to seek work after study). Sweden sets no fixed weekly hour cap on student work during study, provided studies come first.
sweden.tagline: Sweden combines innovation-led education with a strong focus on sustainability.

norway.visaNotes: The visa process involves securing an admission letter, showing proof of funds of ~NOK 137,907 for the year, arranging health insurance, applying for a student residence permit, providing biometrics at a VFS centre, and registering after arrival. Since autumn 2023, non-EU students pay tuition at Norwegian public universities.
norway.languageNotes: Bachelor's applicants need 12 years of schooling plus, often, one year of study, and IELTS 6.0–6.5 or TOEFL; IELTS 6.5 is required for most master's programmes.
norway.costNotes: Bachelor's tuition (non-EU) is NOK 130,000–220,000/yr and master's tuition (non-EU) is NOK 150,000–320,000/yr (approx. €11,000–28,000); the semester fee is ~NOK 700; proof of funds required is ~NOK 137,907/yr; estimated monthly cost of living total is ~NOK 12,000 (students need NOK 12,000–15,000/month).
norway.workRights: Graduates can obtain a 1-year Post-Study Permit (residence permit to seek work after study), with a route to convert to a work permit once employed. Students may work up to 20 hours a week during term time with a work permit.
norway.tagline: Norway offers research-led education with strengths in energy, marine and sustainability.

uae.visaNotes: The sponsoring university arranges the student visa: after offer acceptance the university sponsors the visa, the student completes a medical test and Emirates ID, receives an entry permit, and stamps a residence visa on arrival, alongside mandatory health insurance.
uae.languageNotes: English is the language of instruction across branch campuses; Bachelor's applicants need IELTS 5.5–6.5 (or equivalent) and Master's applicants need IELTS 6.0–6.5.
uae.costNotes: Tuition ranges AED 40,000–100,000/yr (international branch-campus tuition): Undergraduate AED 40,000–75,000/yr, Postgraduate/Master's AED 55,000–100,000/yr, Foundation/diploma AED 30,000–45,000/yr. Living costs (Dubai) are AED 40,000–60,000/yr, with an estimated monthly total of ~AED 4,500–6,500. Proof of funds for the visa is ~AED 30,000. Many campuses offer merit scholarships of 10–30%.
uae.workRights: Graduates get a 12-month post-study grace period to find work, plus a self-sponsored Green Visa (5 years) and a GPA-based Golden Visa (10 years) for outstanding graduates; part-time work during study is permitted with university/free-zone approval.
uae.tagline: The UAE combines globally recognised branch-campus degrees with tax-free careers and long-term visas.

universities: University of Europe for Applied Sciences
germany.visaNotes: Indian applicants need an APS certificate (mandatory academic document verification), an official university admission letter, and a blocked account (Sperrkonto) of €11,904 for the visa year; they then apply for the National (long-stay/D) student visa via VFS with valid health insurance, and after arrival complete address registration (Anmeldung) and convert to a residence permit.
germany.languageNotes: For public universities (EPA route), German is the official language though English-taught master's programmes are widely available; Bachelor's needs IELTS 6.0–6.5/TOEFL (or German B1–B2 for German-taught courses) and Master's needs IELTS 6.5/TOEFL (German proficiency required for German-taught master's, GRE/GMAT for some programmes). For private universities (GAC route), English is the language of instruction throughout, with IELTS 6.0–6.5 for Bachelor's and IELTS 6.5 for Master's (GMAT for some MBAs).
germany.costNotes: EPA (public universities): tuition is €0 in most states, plus a semester contribution of €150–350 (Baden-Württemberg charges non-EU students €1,500/semester); estimated living costs are ~€934/month (typical range €930–1,100/month). GAC (private universities): tuition is €7,000–20,000/yr overall, broken down as Bachelor's €7,000–12,000/yr, Master's €10,000–20,000/yr, MBA €15,000–30,000 (full programme), and Foundation/pathway €5,000–9,000/yr; estimated living costs are ~€950–1,300/month. Both routes require a blocked account (Sperrkonto) of €11,904 (2026) as proof of funds, with a visa blocked-account monthly release rate of €992.
germany.workRights: Graduates get an 18-month job-seeker permit to find work after graduation. The EU Blue Card route applies from €45,934/yr (shortage roles) or €50,700/yr (standard) under 2026 thresholds, and Blue Card holders can qualify for permanent residence in as little as 21–33 months. During study, international students may work 140 full or 280 half days per year (about 20 hours a week).
germany.tagline: Germany pairs tuition-free public universities, strong on theory and industry links, with English-taught career-focused private options, both offering an 18-month post-study work window.

universities: The Hague University of Applied Sciences
netherlands.visaNotes: Non-EU students need an entry visa (MVV) and residence permit, which the university/institution applies for on the student's behalf; applicants must show proof of funds of approximately €13,200/yr (EPA route) or ~€13,000/yr (GAC route), arrange health insurance, and register with the municipality after arrival.
netherlands.languageNotes: Dutch is the official language, but most master's programmes are taught in English (EPA route), and English is the language of instruction across the applied-sciences/private programmes (GAC route); bachelor's typically requires IELTS 6.0–6.5 (or TOEFL for English-taught courses), and master's requires IELTS 6.5 with no band below 6.0, with GMAT required for some MBA/business programmes.
netherlands.costNotes: EPA (public route): undergraduate (non-EU) tuition is €8,000–15,000/yr, postgraduate (non-EU) €11,000–20,000/yr, Universities of Applied Sciences €7,000–12,000/yr, the EU statutory rate is ~€2,700/yr, proof of funds ~€13,200/yr, and estimated cost of living ~€1,100/month. GAC (full-fee route): applied sciences (hbo, non-EU) tuition is €8,000–12,000/yr, private universities €10,000–20,000/yr, hospitality/specialist €11,000–16,000/yr, foundation/pathway €7,000–10,000/yr, proof of funds ~€13,000/yr, and estimated cost of living ~€1,100–1,500/month.
netherlands.workRights: Non-EU students may work part-time with a permit during study (16 hours/week, or full-time in summer, per the GAC brochure), and graduates can stay on a 1-year Orientation Year (zoekjaar) visa to search for work, with a fast, employer-sponsored Highly Skilled Migrant work permit available and a Dutch degree recognised across the EU.
netherlands.tagline: The Netherlands offers English-taught, career-focused degrees at strong public universities.

switzerland.visaNotes: Non-EU students apply for a National (D) visa at the consulate after accepting their offer, must show proof of funds of approximately CHF 21,000/yr, submit documents and biometrics, and register with the canton upon arrival.
switzerland.languageNotes: Programmes are taught in English, German, French or Italian; bachelor's requires IELTS 6.0–6.5 (or a German/French language certificate) and master's requires IELTS 6.5 or language proof, with a strong academic record required for ETH Zurich/EPFL.
switzerland.costNotes: EPA (public route): ETH Zurich/EPFL tuition is CHF 1,460/yr, cantonal universities CHF 1,500–4,000/yr, Universities of Applied Sciences CHF 1,500–5,000/yr, living costs CHF 21,000–27,000/yr, and proof of funds ~CHF 21,000/yr. GAC (private/hospitality route): public university tuition is CHF 1,500–4,000/yr, Universities of Applied Sciences CHF 1,500–5,000/yr, private hospitality schools CHF 25,000–40,000/yr, living costs CHF 21,000–27,000/yr, and proof of funds ~CHF 21,000/yr; both brochures estimate monthly cost of living at ~CHF 1,700–2,300.
switzerland.workRights: Students may work 15 hours a week during term time, and graduates get a 6-month job-search stay to find work with the labour-market test waived for Swiss graduates; hospitality programmes (GAC route) build in paid internship placements.
switzerland.tagline: Switzerland's public universities offer excellent research at very low tuition; the fees stay modest, so living costs are the main expense.

denmark.visaNotes: Accept your offer, show proof of funds of around DKK 80,328 for living costs, and apply for the student residence permit through SIRI followed by biometrics; register for a CPR number and health card on arrival.
denmark.languageNotes: English is widely spoken and many degrees are taught in English.
denmark.costNotes: Non-EU tuition is DKK 45,000-90,000/year for a Bachelor's and DKK 65,000-120,000/year for a Master's (business schools like CBS at the top of that range); living costs around DKK 80,000/year. Non-EU students pay full tuition - Denmark is not tuition-free. Danish Government and university scholarships reduce tuition for strong applicants. Figures indicative; verify per intake.
denmark.workRights: Students may work 20 hours a week (full-time in June-August). Graduates can stay on an establishment card for up to 3 years to seek and take work, with skilled-route permits for shortage and higher-paid roles.
denmark.tagline: Denmark pairs English-taught, innovation-led degrees with one of Europe's most generous post-study work windows.

belgium.visaNotes: Non-EU students show proof of funds of around €8,600/year for the long-stay student visa. Figures indicative; verify per intake.
belgium.languageNotes: A growing range of master's degrees are taught in English; Dutch, French and German are the national languages.
belgium.costNotes: Public tuition is €900-5,000/year, with non-EU rates varying by community (Flemish, French or German-speaking); proof of funds around €8,600/year. Figures indicative; verify per intake.
belgium.workRights: Graduates can use a 12-month search year to find work after study.
belgium.tagline: Belgium blends low-fee, world-ranked universities with a central EU location and a post-study search year.

portugal.visaNotes: Non-EU students show proof of funds of around €9,120/year. A job-seeker residence pathway is available after study. Figures indicative; verify per intake.
portugal.languageNotes: A growing range of degrees are taught in English.
portugal.costNotes: Public non-EU tuition is €3,000-7,000/year for a Bachelor's and €3,000-8,000/year for a Master's; business and specialist programmes are higher. Proof of funds around €9,120/year. Figures indicative; verify per intake.
portugal.workRights: Graduates can use a job-seeker residence pathway to find work after study.
portugal.tagline: Portugal blends affordable, English-taught degrees with a safe lifestyle and a growing tech economy.

czech-republic.visaNotes: Non-EU students show proof of funds of around CZK 120,000/year and apply for a long-stay student visa at the consulate, then register with the foreign police on arrival.
czech-republic.languageNotes: Study in Czech is free, while English-taught programmes charge modest tuition.
czech-republic.costNotes: Czech-taught degrees are free; English-taught programmes charge €2,000-10,000/year for a Bachelor's and €3,000-15,000/year for a Master's, with English-taught General Medicine higher. Proof of funds around CZK 120,000/year. Czech Government and university scholarships support strong international students. Figures indicative; verify per intake.
czech-republic.workRights: Students may work alongside study. Graduates can extend their residence for up to 9 months to seek work, with an Employee Card as a combined work-and-residence route.
czech-republic.tagline: The Czech Republic offers free Czech-taught degrees and low-fee English programmes in a safe, central-European setting.

malta.visaNotes: Non-EU students show proof of funds of around €14,000 for the year and apply for the national (long-stay) student visa, then apply for a residence card after arrival.
malta.languageNotes: English is an official language and the medium of instruction.
malta.costNotes: Tuition at the public University of Malta is around €1,000-11,000/year; proof of funds around €14,000/year. Figures indicative; verify per intake.
malta.workRights: Students may work 20 hours a week after 13 weeks of study. Graduates can apply for a work permit once employed, with a Single Permit combining work and residence.
malta.tagline: Malta offers English-taught, affordable EU degrees on a safe, sunny Mediterranean island.

malaysia.visaNotes: Non-EU students show proof of funds of around RM 30,000 for the student pass. Figures indicative.
malaysia.languageNotes: English is widely used and is the medium of instruction.
malaysia.costNotes: Branch and private-campus tuition is RM 30,000-70,000/year for a Bachelor's and RM 25,000-90,000/year for a Master's (medicine higher); living costs RM 24,000-36,000/year; proof of funds around RM 30,000. A 6% service tax applies to private-university tuition from 2025. Merit scholarships are widely available. Figures indicative.
malaysia.workRights: Students may work up to 20 hours a week during breaks and holidays over 7 days. Graduates can apply for a 12-month Graduate Pass after study.
malaysia.tagline: Malaysia offers UK and Australian branch-campus degrees at a fraction of the cost, close to India.

south-korea.visaNotes: Non-EU students show proof of funds of around ₩20,000,000. Figures indicative; verify per intake.
south-korea.languageNotes: A growing range of English-taught degrees are available, especially in STEM and business.
south-korea.costNotes: Tuition is ₩4M-8M/year for a Bachelor's and ₩5M-12M/year for a Master's (STEM/specialist higher); proof of funds around ₩20,000,000. Most universities offer 30-100% scholarships on top of the GKS (Global Korea Scholarship), which covers full tuition, a monthly stipend, flights and insurance. Figures indicative; verify per intake.
south-korea.workRights: Students may work around 20 hours a week with permission and adequate grades. Graduates can use the D-10 job-seeking visa for up to 1 year to find work after graduation.
south-korea.tagline: South Korea pairs world-class tech universities and fully funded scholarships with a strong graduate job market.

cyprus.visaNotes: Non-EU students show funds for tuition and living; the university guides the student-visa application, with a temporary residence permit (pink slip) after arrival.
cyprus.languageNotes: Universities teach in English, with a growing international community.
cyprus.costNotes: Private-university tuition is €7,000-12,500/year; proof of funds around €7,000/year. Figures indicative; verify per intake.
cyprus.workRights: Students may work 20 hours a week after 6 months in eligible sectors. Graduates can apply for an employer-sponsored work permit once employed.
cyprus.tagline: Cyprus offers English-taught, affordable EU degrees on a safe, sunny Mediterranean island.

spain.visaNotes: Non-EU students show proof of funds of around €7,200/year for the student visa. Figures indicative; verify per intake.
spain.languageNotes: A growing range of English-taught degrees are available in business, STEM and social sciences.
spain.costNotes: Public-university non-EU tuition is €3,000-8,000/year for a Bachelor's and €4,000-12,000/year for a Master's (medicine higher); living costs €8,000-12,000/year; proof of funds around €7,200/year. The state subsidises most of the cost even for non-EU students, and MAEC-AECID and university scholarships reduce it further. Figures indicative; verify per intake.
spain.workRights: Students may work up to 30 hours a week. Graduates can use a 12-24 month job-search visa to stay and find work or start a business.
spain.tagline: Spain's public universities offer affordable, subsidised degrees with a long post-study job-search window.
